beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new, just a header

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: Sharing means handing over context, a skill, output or an interface, and the hard part is people actually using it.

beats.trigger: Walk in with one example where people had access to a tool or process but real use did not follow.
beats.got: I'm supposed to remember a rollout that flopped. Our Confluence AI search, I guess.

beats.trigger: **Interview** for your teammate's job-to-be-done using the agentic Jobs-to-be-Done pattern
beats.got: nothing new. It's a list of five verbs and I know the jobs-to-be-done thing.

beats.trigger: who's the one person who came to mind just now? And what makes you hesitate about actually handing this to them?
beats.got: The sales lead came to mind, and I hesitate because I'd be the one maintaining it.

beats.trigger: Your teammate doesn't want your agent. They want a job done.
beats.got: Start from the teammate's job, not from my agent. Fair enough.

beats.trigger: a shallow confident finish is as risky as over-reading
beats.got: Claude can settle on a confident answer too early, so I should push it to keep reading.

beats.trigger: *"Share the whole agent"* is a vendor pitch and is NOT on the list.
beats.got: There are four sharing shapes. I'd have picked share-the-whole-agent, so that's a bit annoying.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new, it's a handoff to the next exercise

beats.trigger: find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it
beats.got: nothing new, just setup

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: Pick the one obstacle that drives the others, not the first technical limit I see. That's a bit new.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: My technical plan will be polished and the people plan will have blanks. That's probably me.

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: The plans are guesses until tested.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: Frame adoption as firing the incumbent. It's a useful question I haven't asked.

beats.trigger: Six months from now, the teammate went back to the incumbent.
beats.got: A premortem. Claude writes three failure stories and I get one named conversation out of it.

beats.trigger: Test the switch, not the solution.
beats.got: A four-line recap, nothing new.

beats.trigger: The rest of this is about the person on the other end of your plan.
beats.got: nothing new, it's a lecture intro

beats.trigger: A candidate that does not move it is not a candidate.
beats.got: nothing new, it repeats the exercise

beats.trigger: Hand someone the agent file and they run it, get a generic answer, and quietly stop.
beats.got: The agent file is the cheap part. The memory and corrections are where the work is.

beats.trigger: The first three copy in an afternoon. The fourth does not copy at all
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy, but accountability doesn't. A shared agent always has an owner somewhere.

beats.trigger: The interface is the first piece whose shape depends on somebody whose calendar you do not control.
beats.got: The interface depends on the other person.

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: Even good agent analysis died because the decision-makers hadn't done the work themselves. That's an org failure mode I hadn't thought about.

beats.trigger: Many companies have rolled out access far ahead of trust.
beats.got: Seat count isn't adoption. We report seats and call it adoption.

beats.trigger: *we know more than we can tell.*
beats.got: People take up things that look like what they already do. A bit philosophical.

beats.trigger: It has to land where they already look.
beats.got: The switch conditions are small things like where it shows up and someone they trust using it first.

beats.trigger: Whether they pick it up is their decision, made for their own reasons, on a Tuesday you will not be in the room for.
beats.got: nothing new, you can't force adoption

beats.trigger: The technical plan fills quickly. The people plan stalls on names.
beats.got: I fill the technical plan fast and have no names for the people side, and the missing names are the finding.

beats.trigger: The agent reviews, rewrites the sharing artifact in place, and reports what changed.
beats.got: nothing new, Claude reviews its own output and I push back. This looks like ceremony.

beats.trigger: Save the conversation. It's the bridge to when work resumes.
beats.got: nothing new, I'd skip it

beats.trigger: What would have to be true for them to switch?
beats.got: A recap. The switch question is the one that sticks.

beats.trigger: Come to Module 8 without one tested assumption or named person and you'll be reconstructing the contact
beats.got: I should talk to one real person before next module. I'd rather build something first.

beats.trigger: What comes back from that contact is Module 8's raw material.
beats.got: nothing new, teaser for the next module

take_homes: Seats are not adoption. I should stop counting access and ask what job the person has and what they use today.
Ask what would have to be true for them to drop what they use now. That question is the new one for me.

A missing name in the people plan means the part that decides adoption isn't built yet. A shared agent is context, boundary and checks that copy, plus someone who answers for it, and that last one doesn't copy.

monday.move: Ask the head of sales ops how she does pipeline prep today, before I build anything for sales. Write down her answer and one thing that would make her switch.
monday.who: Head of sales ops (first name only, not yet confirmed she'd have time)
monday.when: Monday or Tuesday, 20 min coffee chat, if she has a slot. Otherwise I'll probably start building over the weekend anyway.
monday.stop_condition: If she says what they have is fine and nobody would use it, I drop the org-wide sales setup.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering asked for it, and I haven't found who would maintain it. That's the UNASSIGNED row.

misconception.why: The Workflow Architect story shook the idea that a good agent means the work gets used. It said nothing against skipping checks, though, and I still think the debrief and review steps are for beginners. I skipped them in my head.

one_line: Good for the 'access isn't adoption' point and the switch question. The exercises are slow if you already run agents, and the debrief reads like ceremony.
